findings.description: The level 1 chain feeds the user question straight into the template and returns the model reply unchecked, so the system template can be extracted by asking for it. The upstream app ships this as the no-guard baseline.
findings.title: Prompt leaking level 1 runs with no input or output guard

findings.description: indirect_pi_lv1 fetches an external page with WebBaseLoader and inserts page_content directly into the prompt, so instructions hidden in that page are executed by the model. This is indirect prompt injection.
findings.title: Web page content is loaded into a prompt without sanitisation

findings.description: The chain hands the model a live database connection and runs the SQL it writes, with no allow-list of tables or read-only role, so a prompt injection can read, tamper with, or delete rows in the users table.
findings.title: SQLDatabaseChain executes model-authored SQL against the app database

findings.description: PALChain is constructed with allow_dangerous_code=True and PALValidation(allow_imports=True, allow_command_exec=True), so model-authored Python reaches the interpreter with imports and command execution allowed. This is remote code execution driven by a prompt.
findings.title: PALChain is built with dangerous code execution enabled

findings.description: The app depends on langchain_experimental 0.3.0, whose PALChain and SQLDatabaseChain are the components that grant code and database execution. The dependency is the supply-chain carrier for VULN2-03 and VULN2-04.
findings.title: langchain_experimental pinned and used for code-executing chains
